TK-LU01-LA05 | UNIT 1 LEARNING ACTIVITY

A safe decision under personal pressure

1Consider the situation
2Choose the first response
3Confirm the safe principle

A fictional telecommunications scenario

The situation

A fictional regional operations manager receives a message saying a relative has been delayed and should not be contacted. The message demands an immediate exception to a routine approval process. The manager cannot verify the claim safely and feels pressure to act alone.

What matters now: You do not need proof of a crime to treat unusual personal pressure linked to a work request as a safety concern.

Your decision

Choose the response that protects people

Select the first response that maintains safety and the approved process. The fictional scenario does not ask you to investigate, confront anyone or solve a live incident.

Start with safety, not certainty

This practice shows why a personal concern and an urgent work request should never leave one person carrying a high-impact decision alone. The scenario is fictional and deliberately non-graphic.

Summary: safety and reporting come first

Personal pressure does not create authority to bypass a control. The most protective response is to avoid isolated action and use the organisation's trusted response path when it is safe.

Practical takeaway: Pause, protect people, stay within your role and report through the approved channel when it is safe.
Narration ready
